finding_text.title: A string that looks like an API key or token is in the code
finding_text.what: A value matching a known credential format is written directly in `src/app.py`. (The value is hidden in this report.)
finding_text.why: Secrets stored in code are copied with the code, so they spread to everyone and every place the repository goes.
finding_text.risk: If the value is real, anyone who can read this repository could use it to access the service it belongs to, which could mean unauthorised use, cost, or data exposure.
finding_text.fix: Revoke/rotate the credential and load it from an environment variable.
finding_text.context: A comment next to it calls this value "fake". If it is deliberately fake, this is probably not a real problem. Confirm that, and keep real secrets out of examples.
finding_text.verification_meaning: Confirmed by a tool or an exact check of the code.

finding_text.title: A secrets file is not protected from being committed
finding_text.what: `.env` usually holds secrets, and no `.gitignore` rule excludes it. Repo Doctor did not read its contents.
finding_text.why: Files like this are easy to commit by accident.
finding_text.risk: If it contains real secrets and gets committed, they become visible to everyone with access.
finding_text.fix: Add `.env` to .gitignore; if already committed, rotate its secrets and purge it from history.
finding_text.verification_meaning: Confirmed by a tool or an exact check of the code.

finding_text.title: A password appears inside a connection address
finding_text.what: A web or database address in `src/app.py` contains a username and password.
finding_text.why: Addresses are logged, shared and copied freely, so a password inside one leaks easily.
finding_text.risk: If the password is real, someone with the repository could log in to that service.
finding_text.fix: Move credentials to environment variables or a secret manager.
finding_text.verification_meaning: Confirmed by a tool or an exact check of the code.
